label: Composite secondary index
type: a secondary index on two or more document fields, where key ORDER is significant - it determines which predicates can produce a span and whether ORDER BY can be pushed down. A specialisation of index-type:secondary-index (already promoted); not a separate mechanism from it.
recurrence_note: Ten files discounted to 5 independent sources - the best-attested concept promoted this round. The ten collapse to five because four of the page-families involved exist in two or three trees each: create-index (guide), covering-indexes, groupby-aggregate-performance, index-scans and indexing-and-query-perf. Five distinct authored pages is a strong count by this project's standards even after the discount.
note: PROMOTED. The load-bearing fact is that key order is part of the index's identity, not a detail of how it was typed: the same fields in a different order are a different index for every purpose the module discusses. This is what makes index-type:composite-secondary-index worth a record rather than being left as 'a secondary index with more keys'.
relates_to_competency_question: What kinds of index can I create, and which of my queries can each one serve?
